# Who Can See Your AI Notebook at Work? A Plain-Language Guide to Audit Logs

> **In short:** Google Workspace admins can now see detailed logs of how Gemini Notebook is used inside their organization — including who created, edited, or shared which notes. For employees, this means your AI notes at work are not private from your IT team.

If you have ever jotted something sensitive into a work AI assistant — a draft resignation letter, a private complaint about your boss, notes from a doctor's appointment you took between meetings — you may want to know who, if anyone, can see them. That question just got a clearer answer for anyone using Google Workspace with Gemini.

## What just changed

Google has added **audit logs** (think of them as a detailed activity diary kept by the IT team) for Gemini Notebook inside the Workspace Admin console. Until recently, admins could see broad usage numbers — "yes, someone in your company is using this tool" — but not much detail.

The new logs let admins see specific events: when a notebook was created, when it was edited, when it was shared, and similar actions. Admins can also review these events inside the **Audit and Investigation tool** — basically the search bar IT uses to look back at what happened in the company account.

For most employees, this won't change their day. For people who treat AI notebooks like private scratchpads, it matters.

## What an audit log actually is

The phrase sounds technical, but the idea is simple. Every time you do something on a work account — send an email, upload a file, create a document — the system quietly keeps a small receipt. That receipt usually includes:

- **Who** did it (your account)
- **What** they did (created a file, shared a link)
- **When** it happened (date and time)
- Sometimes **where** it happened (IP address — the unique identifier of the network you were on)

Admins normally use these logs to investigate security incidents: "Did anyone in our company click that phishing link last Tuesday?" or "Who accessed the spreadsheet with customer data before it leaked?"

Until now, Gemini Notebook activity was mostly invisible to that investigation process. Now it shows up the same way email or Drive activity does.

## What this means for you

- **If you're an everyday employee**: assume anything you write in Gemini Notebook at work can be reviewed by your IT or compliance team, especially if there's ever an investigation. This isn't new for email or Drive — it's just now true for AI notes too.
- **If you're a people manager**: this is a good moment to remind your team what work AI tools are and aren't for. A friendly tip in your next 1:1 ("just so you know, these notes aren't private") goes further than a policy doc nobody reads.
- **If you're an admin or IT lead**: you now have a clearer picture of how AI notebooks are being used across your organization. That's useful for spotting risky sharing (someone making a notebook public by accident), unusual access patterns, or just understanding which teams are getting real value from the tool.
- **If you're job-hunting or dealing with something sensitive**: keep personal, private, or legally delicate writing out of work AI tools. Use your personal accounts, a paper notebook, or your phone's notes app for anything you wouldn't want a future employer — yours or someone else's — to read.

## A small habit that prevents big headaches

Before you start a new notebook in any work AI tool, take ten seconds to ask yourself: *"If my company's IT team had to show my manager what I wrote here, would I be fine with that?"*

If the answer is yes, carry on. If it's no, move it somewhere private. That one question — before the first prompt — saves you from having to delete, explain, or worry later.

## Wrap-up

Audit logs aren't there to spy on you. They're there so your company can investigate real problems when they happen. The new Gemini Notebook logs simply bring AI notes into line with the same visibility that email and Drive have had for years. The practical takeaway is small but worth keeping in mind: treat work AI tools like work email — useful, helpful, and visible to the people whose job it is to look after the company's accounts.
